The homepage at www.cybl.ca (SportsEngine platform) publicly renders two full team directories, 'Middle School Teams' and 'High School Teams', which we captured above (~30 middle-school + ~35 high-school entries; some are duplicate club names appearing in both tiers, e.g. YvY Elite, Team Sanctuary, Ottawa Elite). Two ambiguities to flag: (1) 'Simcoe United' and 'Barrie Royals/Simcoe Muskoka' may be the SAME regional franchise described two different ways (both draw from Barrie/Simcoe County) rather than two separate ones - needs a human check; (2) Kingston Impact is ALSO an EOBA member club (see above) - a clean example of one parent club running programs across two different leagues (EOBA house/rep AND the JUEL provincial girls league), which is exactly the kind of cross-league parent->program relationship you asked us to flag. We were not able to pin down a 12th franchise (Welland/Niagara beyond Pelham, and Etobicoke/North York were mentioned only as competition VENUES in a Simcoe United schedule, not as confirmed separate franchise names).

summary: All 10 named leagues/circuits are real (Phoenix League's exact name did not exist as such, but a clear, high-confidence match - 'Phoenix Hoops' / 'Phoenix Basketball League' - was identified with by far the richest team data of the whole set, 50+ clubs across 3 seasons, all from fully public Exposure Events /teams pages). Best data yields, in order: Phoenix League (public Exposure Events season pages, no login, 50+ real club/team names across Winter+Spring 2025+Spring 2026), CYBL (public SportsEngine homepage renders full Middle School + High School team directories, ~65 names, despite deep standings/about permalinks 404ing), ORBL (fully public in-house PHP pages, both a 2025-26 season list - now mostly IEM's own branch network - and an older 2019-20 list with real outside clubs), EOBA (About page + one division page gave ~16 clubs/abbreviations, several expandable to full names, but the master 30-club list and full standings live behind a TeamSnap JS app we could not read), JUEL (~11 of 12 franchises reconstructed piecemeal from individual club sites/Instagram, no central directory exists). Weakest/blocked: Hoop City (tourneymachine.com 403'd, LeagueApps portal rendered empty for us - only 3 names surfaced via Instagram), Toronto Big League (own domain refused every connection attempt from our tooling, Exposure Events season listing 410 Gone - likely a transient reach issue on our end worth a human recheck rather than confirmed dead), TCBL (confirmed as Toronto Community/Chinese Basketball League, a 200+ team MEN'S league whose youth arm is actually branded 'J17 Basketball' - a good redirect for future research - but tcbl.ca itself is a JS app we couldn't read; also explicitly ruled out a false-positive 'TCBL' that turned out to be Virginia's Tidewater Catholic Basketball League), Kingdom Summer League (Instagram-only presence confirmed exactly as briefed, ~14K followers, but no website/Exposure Events/TourneyMachine footprint found, and searches kept colliding with an unrelated much-larger Columbus, Ohio league of the same name which we excluded), Canada Hoops Circuit (operators and Ontario regional director confirmed, but no page we reached renders actual Summit/Nationals team rosters - Instagram is the likely next lead). Notable parent-club -> program relationships spotted (beyond the already-known Northern Kings/Cali Prep): North Toronto Basketball + Scarborough Blues jointly run the GTA JUEL/JUEL Prep franchise as a named collaboration; Kingston Impact runs programs in BOTH EOBA (house/rep) and JUEL (provincial girls); ORBL's 2025-26 season appears to now be run almost entirely by IEM Basketball's own multi-branch network (Newmarket/Aurora/East Gwillimbury/Bradford/King City/North York) rather than outside independent clubs, a marked change from its 2019-20 roster of genuinely separate clubs; and TCBL (adult men's league) sponsors/points to J17 Basketball as its distinct youth-facing brand. No logins or access controls were bypassed - every 'blocked' or 'dead' verdict above reflects a 403/410/empty-shell response or unreachable host, reported as-is.
